data.reasoning: The package is a standard binary distribution (-bin) that fetches precompiled releases from the project's own GitHub repository with SHA256 checksum verification. The PKGBUILD contains only variable assignments and standard packaging functions (prepare/package) with no command substitution, eval, or network operations in global scope. The wrapper script simply changes directory and executes the installed binary. The .desktop file is a standard launcher entry. All sources are pinned to specific GitHub release tags with checksums, closing the swap risk. No injection patterns detected.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool errors in the qwen model (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when reviewing PKGBUILD and .desktop files, resulting in an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found them safe. The openrouter/free report (advisory only, not counted as vote) also found the package safe. This is not a genuine security disagreement but rather a tool failure.
coverage_issues: qwen model experienced API errors (HTTP 400) for PKGBUILD and DK64Recompiled-bin.desktop reviews, resulting in incomplete coverage
learnings: API errors should trigger automatic retry or fallback to prevent inconclusive verdicts when the package structure is straightforward
Initial PKGBUILD audit (for makepkg --printsrcinfo safety) should be distinguished from full file review - the qwen model passed the initial audit but failed the full review due to API errors
Binary packages (-bin) with pinned GitHub release sources and checksums are low-risk and should be prioritized for faster processing
